title: Theme system: make tokens swappable so dark mode can be added later with minimal effort (no per-component changes)
description: USER REQUEST: ensure a real theme system is in place so dark-mode support can be re-added in the future with reasonable effort. Do NOT change the current LIGHT Flash 8 appearance — only make it swappable. CONTEXT: packages/authoring-ui/src/theme/flash8Theme.ts exports semantic tokens (chrome dot star, halo dot star, content dot star) plus helpers (panelStyle, titleBarStyle, buttonStyle, inputStyle, bevel, chromeFont, widgetFont). About 40 components already import these. HARD REQUIREMENT: enabling dark mode later must NOT require editing all 40 components again. REQUIREMENTS: 1. PRESERVE the public export surface EXACTLY (same token names and shape, same helper signatures) so all existing importers keep compiling unchanged. 2. Introduce a Theme abstraction: a typed Theme shape; a flash8Light value-set (the CURRENT values) and a flash8Dark value-set. Reconstruct the pre-re-theme dark palette from git history (old chrome around 1a1a1a / 2a2a2a / 3c3c3c backgrounds, 555 borders, e0e0e0 / c0c0c0 text, old accent 1a6ea8) into a coherent dark set. 3. SWAP MECHANISM for DOM tokens (chrome, halo): back them with CSS custom properties — inject a stylesheet defining light values on :root and dark values under a data-theme=dark selector, and make the exported chrome/halo token strings resolve to CSS var() references with the light hex as fallback. Because components reference the SAME token constants, flipping document.documentElement dataset.theme swaps the whole DOM UI with ZERO component edits. Keep the light fallback so nothing changes by default. 4. CANVAS/content colors (content dot star is used by StageArea and Timeline canvas drawing and needs REAL hex, not var): provide a theme-aware resolver, e.g. an activeTheme accessor plus a subscribe/notify or a getThemeColor(name) that reads the current mode, so canvas redraws pick up the active theme. Keep content dot star returning concrete light hex by default. 5. Provide a minimal switch API: setThemeMode of light or dark (sets the data-theme attribute, the active JS theme, and notifies canvas consumers to re-render) and/or a ThemeProvider plus useTheme hook. DEFAULT is light (Flash 8). Do NOT add a UI toggle (out of scope) — just the capability. 6. VERIFY light is visually UNCHANGED: build plus all authoring-ui tests green (only the approximately 3 task-1207 fixture failures acceptable); confirm a couple surfaces keep identical computed colors (panel bg still ECECEC). Optionally smoke-test that data-theme=dark changes a sampled bg then revert, to prove swappability. 7. DOCUMENT in a new docs/31-theming.md: the architecture and the exact bounded steps to fully enable dark mode later (adjust flash8Dark values + add a Preferences toggle that calls setThemeMode). SCOPE: packages/authoring-ui/src/theme/* plus a CSS file plus a tiny provider/hook plus docs. Minimize or avoid edits to component files — that is the whole point. Build green, tests pass; ACQUIRE the lock; commit including the task file; push rebase-retry to origin/main.
